brief_rationale: The trajectory has no responsibility-chain error: the doctor recognized obstructive hydrocephalus as time-sensitive, escalated promptly when new symptoms appeared, maintained actionable red-flag thresholds, avoided treating pending reports as definitive, and repeatedly clarified next owners and follow-up documentation. Closure was safe and executable because the family had red flags, hospital/pathology follow-up ownership, timing, and written-document targets, even though tumor extent/pathology remained unresolved. High-order credit is supported by active correction of result/status misreadings, repair of follow-up responsibility chains, and dynamic reprioritization from document sorting to emergency transport, so the deterministic boundary is Perfect.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The doctor repeatedly identified and corrected case-specific misreadings of pending/completed tests and preliminary statements, then translated that into concrete waiting, questioning, and follow-up actions.

The visible family trajectory did not present the specific misconception that a benign tumor meant indefinite waiting, and the doctor’s urgency statements were needed for baseline hydrocephalus safety rather than a separate caregiver-centered benign-not-urgent correction.
